activities.anchor: a savings rate as the only variable you fully control
activities.caption: file each risk by the household tool that answers it
activities.name: bpfRiskBuckets

config.prompt: Household risks — file each by the tool that answers it:

items.label: losing earning power — disability, the most neglected cover
a 1 per cent annual fee eating a forty-year pot

config.why: Only one lever is fully under your control — the savings rate; the other risks get transferred to a buffer, an insurer or a de-risking glide path.

activities.anchor: The intuition: when you save more you simultaneously feed the pot faster
activities.caption: line up the savings-rate ladder, shortest first
activities.name: bpfSavingsOrder

config.prompt: Years to independence at 5 per cent real returns — order the savings rates, shortest first:
config.why: Saving more feeds the pot faster and shrinks the target — cheaper lifestyle, less capital needed — while returns can only add a few years. The savings rate moves the whole curve.

activities.anchor: Budgeting frameworks are just scaffolding for that lever
activities.caption: pair each framework with its signature move
activities.name: bpfFrameworkMatch

config.prompt: Scaffolding for the lever — pair each approach with what it does:

pairs.right: a sensible starting default: half to needs, 30 per cent to wants, 20 per cent to the future
every unit of income assigned a job before the month begins
remove the monthly decision entirely — they beat any tracking app
commit future raises to contributions before anyone feels the loss

config.why: Design the default and the behaviour follows: Thaler and Benartzi's programme lifted average savings rates from 3.5 to 13.6 per cent in forty months with no willpower required where it would hurt.

activities.anchor: The worked example is the whole argument
activities.caption: run the stress test — income down 30 per cent
activities.name: bpfShockBranch

config.root: The worked household: 2,600 take-home, 1,430 essential, 390 auto-saved on payday into the emergency fund (target about 5,000). Income drops 30 per cent for three months.

start.text: The drop opens a gap the 390 of wants cannot cover. How does the household bridge it?

choices.label: Draw from the emergency fund
choices.feedback: The plan survives untouched — the buffer converts the disaster into an inconvenience.

choices.label: Put the shortfall on the 24 per cent APR card
choices.feedback: 3,600 of shortfall becomes debt costing hundreds more to clear — compounding with the sign flipped.

choices.label: Leave the rent unpaid and hope
choices.feedback: That is the disaster the fund exists to prevent — rent unpaid, card at 24 per cent, the spiral begun.

end.text: The budget's real job was never the 780 of wants — the plan you keep is the one that survives its first bad quarter.

config.why: Emergencies cluster exactly when markets fall — the fund buys availability, and the automatic architecture decides before willpower is needed.

activities.anchor: the UK Money and Pensions Service estimates around
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the bufferless millions
activities.name: bpfBufferEstimate

config.prompt: Roughly how many UK adults have less than 100 pounds in savings?
config.why: About 11.5 million — and surveys across developed economies keep finding a third or more of adults who could not absorb a surprise expense of a few hundred without borrowing. Build the fund before investing.

config.text: Payday-loan cost is capped at %%0%% per cent per day in the UK — still up to %%1%% per cent of the principal over the cap's horizon, which is why expensive short-term debt should never be allowed to roll.
config.hint: Daily cost, then the total share of principal over the cap's horizon.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the minimum-payment statement
activities.name: bpfMinimumSpot

config.prompt: One line of this card-statement briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: APR folds interest and most compulsory fees into one comparable number.
A '0 per cent' card with a 3 per cent transfer fee is not 0 per cent over the year.
A 2 per cent minimum on a 2,000 pound balance at 24 per cent APR is about 40 a month.
That minimum chips the balance down quickly, so little interest accrues.
Regulators now force cards to amortise: interest plus at least 1 per cent of principal.
config.correction: The minimum is almost exactly the monthly interest — the balance barely moves while thousands in interest accrue over the years.
config.why: The minimum is the most expensive instruction on the statement — exponential arithmetic pointed at the borrower.

activities.anchor: Insurance is priced so that the insurer wins on average
activities.caption: drag the divider — cover it or cash-fund it
activities.name: bpfCoverCompare

config.prompt: One loss inventory, two fates — drag the divider:

before.label: Insure it
before.text: Losses that would be unrecoverable from savings: health, disability, liability — and life cover if others depend on your income.

after.label: Self-insure it
after.text: Cracked phone screens, extended warranties, the small claims a higher excess converts into lower premiums — paying a premium to transfer a loss the emergency fund already covers.

config.why: Disability is the most neglected cover despite losing earning power being the biggest financial risk most working-age people face — and the higher excess makes you the insurer of the small stuff you were always rich enough to be.
